'''John Edward Allen''' (6 December 1928 – 19 August 2026) was a British engineer and [[plasma physicist]].<ref name="mi">{{cite web| url=https://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/people/john.allen | title=Prof. John E Allen MA, PhD, DEng, DSc | publisher=[[Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford]] | location=UK | accessdate=5 August 2022 }}</ref> In particular, he directly contributed to international [[dusty plasma]] experiments in space under [[microgravity]] conditions.<ref name="franklin13">{{cite journal| url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0022-3727/36/22/e01 | title=Special issue in honour of J E Allen's 75th birthday | editor-first=R. N. | editor-last=Franklin | publisher=[[IOP Publishing]] | journal=[[Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics]] | volume=36 | number=22 | date=2003 | doi=10.1088/0022-3727/36/22/e01 | s2cid=250887458 | url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Education==
Allen gained [[Bachelor of Engineering]] (1949), [[Doctor of Philosophy]] (1953), and [[Doctor of Engineering]] (1963) degrees from the [[University of Liverpool]]. His research included experiments with high-current [[spark discharge]]s involving currents up to
265kA, the highest in any laboratory at the time.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/system/files/users/cvs/career%202010.pdf | title=Professor John Edward Allen – Summary of Research Career | publisher=[[Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford]] | location=UK | date=January 2010 | accessdate=12 November 2022 }}</ref> He also gained a [[Master of Arts]] degree (1964) at the [[University of Cambridge]], and Master of Arts (1965) and [[Doctor of Science]] (1975) degrees at the [[University of Oxford]].<ref name="mi" />

==Career==
During 1952–1958, Allen was a science officer and then senior science officer at the [[Atomic Energy Research Establishment]] (AERE, Harwell). From 1958 to 1964, he was a consultant at the Brazilian [[National Nuclear Energy Commission]] ([[CNEN]]) Laboratory and a professor at the [[Sapienza University of Rome|University of Rome]] in Italy. During 1964–1965, he was an assistant director of research at the University of Cambridge at the invitation of the engineer [[W. R. Hawthorne]]. He spent the major portion of his career as a [[Fellow (college)|Fellow]] of [[University College, Oxford]], from 1965 to 1996.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.univ.ox.ac.uk/news/celebrating-john-allen/ | title=Celebrating John Allen | publisher=[[University College, Oxford]] | location=UK | date=10 January 2019 | accessdate=5 August 2022 }}</ref> He was a [[Reader (academic rank)|Reader]] (1990–1996) and then [[Emeritus Professor]] of [[Engineering Science]] from 1996 in the [[Department of Engineering Science, University of Oxford|Department of Engineering Science]] at University of Oxford, when he became an [[Emeritus Fellow]] of University College. In 1991, he was editor of the book ''Gas Discharge Physics'' with the theoretical physicist [[Yuri Raizer]].<ref>{{cite book| first=Yuri P. | last=Raizer | author-link=Yuri Raizer | editor-first=John E. | editor-last=Allen | title=Gas Discharge Physics | date=1991 | publisher=[[Springer (publisher)|Springer]] | url=https://link.springer.com/book/9783642647604 | isbn=978-3642647604 }}</ref> He had also been a Visiting Professor in [[Physics]] at [[Imperial College London]].<ref name="mi" />

==Fellowships and awards==
Allen was a Fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]] (IoP), the former [[Institution of Electrical Engineers]] (IEE, now part of the [[Institution of Engineering and Technology]]), and the [[American Physical Society]] (APS). He was also a member of the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]] (IEEE) Nuclear and Plasma Society. In 2013, a special issue of the ''[[Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics]]'' was produced in honour of his 75th birthday.<ref name="franklin13" /> In 1998, Allen was awarded the IEE Achievement Medal for Science, Education and Technology.<ref name="ucr98">{{cite magazine| title=Emeritus Fellows: Professor J.E. Allen | magazine=[[University College Record]] | page=13 | date=October 1998 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.theiet.org/media/7598/achieve-winners.pdf | title=The IET Achievement Medals – 1998 | publisher=[[Institution of Engineering and Technology]] | page=4 | work=[[Archive.org]] | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210519221910/https://www.theiet.org/media/7598/achieve-winners.pdf | accessdate=19 May 2021 | archive-date=19 May 2021 }}</ref> He was also awarded the Distinguished Scientist Award by the International Topical Conference on Plasma Science.<ref name="univ">{{cite web| url=https://www.univ.ox.ac.uk/news/distinguished-scientist-award/ | title=Distinguished Scientist Award | publisher=[[University College, Oxford]] | location=UK | date=4 February 2013 | accessdate=5 August 2022 }}</ref>

==Death==
Allen died on 19 August 2026, aged 97.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.univ.ox.ac.uk/news/in-memoriam-professor-john-allen/| title=In Memoriam: Professor John Edward Allen | publisher=[[University College Oxford]] | location=UK | date=25 August 2026 | accessdate=28 August 2026 }}</ref>
